summary: PR 1783 is valid test-only hardening and accurately rejects returned-hidden-state slicing as proof of the ordinary Kimi-K3 generated-reasoning leak. It contains no production fix, the candidate tests already pass on the recorded base, and the original intermittent Kimi-K3 failure remains unverified in the available environment.

tests.what_was_measured: The candidate's complete regression file passes unchanged on base 358c163: 10 passed, 2 subtests. There is no candidate-attributable failing-before/passing-after production change.
The exact candidate regression passes: 10 passed, 2 subtests.

On MI355X/gfx950, 100 randomized packed-offset cases and a two-request ordinary token-commit boundary passed; the harness also captured the zero-row return_hidden_states='last' IndexError as a remaining counterexample.
No native source paths changed; rg exit 1 means no matching path, so a native rebuild was not applicable.

gpu_execution.evidence: Independent adversarial tensor checks ran on one AMD Instinct MI355X with gfx950:sramecc+:xnack- using torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. This does not qualify Kimi-K3 or the reported NVIDIA topology.

remaining_counterexamples: Full capture with return_hidden_states='last' and extend_input_len=0 raises IndexError on an empty hidden-state slice; the candidate's zero-row test uses return_hidden_states=False and misses this combination.
No test generates Kimi-K3 reasoning from distinct prompts, so semantic cross-prompt isolation remains untested.
No candidate test exercises concurrent HTTP requests, eight-way tensor parallelism, NVIDIA B300/CUDA 13, or repeated randomized server scheduling.
remaining_limitations: Kimi-K3 weights and a deterministic request corpus were unavailable.
The environment provides one AMD MI355X/gfx950 GPU with ROCm 7.2 instead of eight NVIDIA B300 GPUs with CUDA 13.0.
The source issue is intermittent and supplies no deterministic reproducer.
The tiny-Llama fixture can qualify transport and engine execution only and cannot validate Kimi-K3 architecture or reasoning semantics.
The official v0.5.17 tag already contains the tested hidden-state offset ordering, so rollback failure is not reproduction of the v0.5.17 report.
